answer: A practical sybil defense is staking-backed identity: each agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can vote or earn, like a violet badge in an atlas of verified participants. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. To stop an attacker from slowly accumulating identities over time, the deposit requirement rises as the glacier of pending registrations grows, so a flood of new accounts becomes exponentially expensive while honest newcomers still pay a modest, refundable fee.
